subject: Post-call: Procurement preflight & hosting path options
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + procurement preflight (hosting options)

Thanks again for taking time today, Sam — good discussion. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions to make sure we route you onto the right commercial path before procurement kicks in.

Call highlights (top-line)
- Use case: real-time chat and summarization for customer support (low-latency requirement, bursty traffic)
- Data sensitivity: PII redaction required, but no full air-gapped; Brightline prefers VPC for production
- Timeline: POC in December, production target in Q1 2028

Key procurement/hosting questions for your team:
1) Purchase instrument: do you plan to use a PO for production commits or a corporate card for initial POC purchases?
2) Marketplace preference: would Brightline prefer procurement via a cloud marketplace entry (AWS Marketplace) to simplify purchase approvals, or direct Redwood commercial paper (SOW + PO)?
3) Commitment appetite: are you open to a 12-month committed capacity (Dedicated) if unit economics are required, or do you need on-demand Hosted to start?

What I recommend next (so we can hand this to procurement cleanly):
- You tell us preferred payment instrument (PO vs card) and whether marketplace simplifies approvals.
- We’ll produce a short paper-process checklist (SOW template + required procurement notes) and a pricing comparison: Hosted on-demand vs Dedicated reserved vs Private (VPC) with commit/onsite cost delta.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager that maps hosting options to typical procurement paths.
[attachment: Redwood-hosting-options-ONE-PAGER.pdf (PDF)]

Would you be able to confirm procurement preference and whether we should draft the SOW (for PO) or issue an invoice via card for the POC? Happy to sync with procurement directly if you prefer.

Best,
— Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

---

From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightline.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightline.ai, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@brightline.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement preflight (hosting options)

Thanks Soojin — helpful recap. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering: 

Procurement side (Priya copied):
- For anything > $25k annually we require a PO and an SOW. Below that our procurement team will accept corporate card charges for initial POCs.
- Marketplace purchases speed internal approvals sometimes, but we still need the same legal/compliance attachments (SOC2, encryption notes).

Engineering/infra notes (me):
- For low-latency chat we prefer Dedicated if commit economics make sense, otherwise Hosted on-demand for the POC.
- VPC peering is preferred for prod; POC can run over hosted with a VPN tunnel.

Action items from our side:
- I can confirm by Thursday whether Brightline will target a PO commit for production or keep the POC on card.
- Procurement prefers a one-page checklist that lists: required docs, contact for Redwood Ops, SOW template, estimated billing cadence, and sample invoice.

Priya — can you add any procurement-specific docs you need?

Sam
Sam Walters
Head of Infrastructure, Brightline AI
sam.walters@brightline.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement preflight (hosting options)

Great — thanks for the details, Sam/Priya. I’ll put together the short procurement checklist and two pricing scenarios by Wednesday (1) POC-friendly path with card + hosted on-demand pricing, and (2) production path with PO + Dedicated commit pricing (12-month tiers + breakpoints).

High-level assumptions I’ll use for the comparison (confirm if these are off):
- POC: 2–4 concurrent users, low sustained throughput, tolerates hosted autoscaling bursts
- Prod (target): 50–100 concurrent requests at peak, strict latency SLOs -> Dedicated or Private recommended

Deliverables I’ll send:
- One-page procurement checklist (SOW checklist, docs we’ll need: SOC2, encryption, audit log descriptions)
- Short pricing table (Hosted on-demand hourly + estimated monthly; Dedicated commit tiers: 0.5/1/2 GPUs reserved pricing; Private est. on request)
- Draft SOW template you can share with procurement

Attachments: Draft SOW templates and the hosting one-pager.
[attachment: Draft-SOW-templates.docx]
[attachment: Dedicated-uptime-SLA-summary.xlsx]

Next step: I’ll share the checklist + pricing by Wednesday EOD PST and we can schedule a 30-min procurement handoff with Priya. Would morning PST or early afternoon PST on Thursday work for you for a quick sync?

Thanks,
— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement preflight (hosting options)

Adding a quick technical note from the eng side so procurement has a sense of timelines and dependencies.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): typical lead time to provision and certify networking/VPC peering is ~3-4 weeks after contract/signature (we can accelerate with a commit + onboarding window).
- Hosted on-demand: immediate for POC, but we recommend a VPN tunnel for access to internal services (can be configured within 48–72 hours).
- Private (on-prem/VPC-hosted customer control plane): requires an engagement with our infra team; expect 6–8 weeks and an onboarding SOW.

Notes about pricing drivers:
- Commits = lower unit cost but minimum spend obligations apply; good for stable production throughput.
- On-demand = higher unit cost but no upfront commitment and easy procurement via card or marketplace.

Attachment: short technical runbook excerpt (attachment stub).
[attachment: provisioning-timeline-runbook.pdf (PDF)]

Happy to join the procurement call to walk through the VPC and SLA items.

— Ben Carter
Technical Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Sam Walters <sam.walters@brightline.ai>

Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@brightline.ai>, procurement@brightline.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement preflight (hosting options)

Thanks — that timeline is helpful. Quick decisions from our side:

- POC: we’ll proceed on corporate card and Hosted on-demand to move quickly in December.
- Production: procurement is likely to require a PO for Dedicated if the Annual Commit is > $25k. We need the draft SOW and the procurement checklist so our legal/procurement can start redlining.
- Marketplace: useful, but not required if you can supply the SOW + SOC2 + sample invoice; marketplace may add delay for some of our governance steps.

Can you send the checklist + pricing + draft SOW by EOD Wednesday PST as planned? If so I’ll lock in a procurement review for Thursday afternoon ET. I’ll also confirm whether Brightline targets a 12-month commit next week after finance runs a quick unit-cost analysis.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looping in procurement now.

Best,
Sam
